Okay, so I made this post, originally for /r/PCMasterrace, but it was removed because it was considered a "Thank god it's over!" post (although it wasn't). But I thought I would make it here, mainly to get it all off my chest, but also in the hopes that the Voat Chaper of the Master Race might heed it's concerns.

In the wake of paid mods, it seems that the PCMR has been a little fractured, with many of the more circlejerk-focused members unfairly criticizing the ones who haven't forgiven Valve and Gaben. One of the mods there suggested that the people who wanted to remove Gabe from the banner were outsiders who came in just to troll and "disrupt the dialogue". When I criticized this statement (as I thought it seemed like an easy way to deligitamize a user's concerns and cast them as an outsider), I was called a "concern troll" by several users and my loyalty to the PCMR was questioned. Now, I've only been subscribed to the Reddit chapter for about two and a half years, but I think that definitely qualifies me as a member of the community. I've always loved the good spirit, friendly help, and even giveaways that the community likes to indulge in and I've always tried to be a part of it. But being shit on by so many members simply for recognizing the fact that Valve is a business and that blind hero worship will just leave us open to another Paid-Mods Scandal has somehow gotten me labeled an instigator or an outsider. This has all been rather disappointing, as I mentioned before, because I love this community.

It's apparent that the paid mods scandal has created a great divide in the PCMR and has fractured the entire gaming and Elder Scrolls communities, in general. Pointing fingers and turning on each other won't help remedy that in the slightest and I think it is unfair to dismiss somebody's concerns outright, even if you don't agree with them. You don't have to agree with me about Valve and GabeN, but you should have to at least hear my concerns as I am a part of the community and should be just as valued as any other member. I welcome criticism, but not McCarthyism.

Yeah, I hope the voat PCMR will promote being factual over being circlejerky. I'm tired of directing people to /r/unixporn when they say that Macs are non-customisable, or telling them for the nth time that Linux does in fact have games.

or telling them for the nth time that Linux does in fact have games.

Oh yeah, this is something that shouldn't be happening anymore. I actually haven't returned to Linux since before Steam started getting all these Linux ports. I think when I finally build my desktop I'll dual boot with either Ubuntu (I just like it) or Steam OS (kinda want to try something new, especially since my desktop will be connected to my TV). I wonder how many of my Steam games have Linux versions built in, now.

I'd say go for SteamOS or even just pure Debian, it's more stable than the *buntu family both from my own experience and from looking at a lot of posts on Linux reddits.

Or you could go all the way and install Arch(or Antergos if you don't have time to configure everything). It's not as hard as it seems really, especially with Antergos.

Over the past few months, I've increased the width of the container as valid complaints have surfaced, but the container layout will no longer be increased for the following reasons:

  • It is now at a length where comment reading is the most comfortable.
  • Increasing the width would break a lot of things, like comments* and settings pages.
  • Increasing the width would start to displace whitespace from the outsides to the middle, rending the entire point of the container null.

At this point, I find no logical reason to increase the container width. It is at a length where it would only displace the whitespace from the outside to the inside (thus not saving much scrolling at all). It would break a lot of layout rules and make Voat look like a 90's site (kind of like Reddit). If you feel that you need that extra real estate on your screen, you should probably take @catechumen's advice and turn your monitor to the portrait orientation.

If, however, anyone feels like this type of site is in anyway comfortable to read, you should probably just get a plugin.

* comments no longer have a max width (unset ever since the zoomable images update), so increasing container width would make the lines way longer than they need to be. It would make things harder to read and messy-looking.
